summary: Court offices are closed on Monday for the Alaska Day observance, which fell on a Sunday this year, and the Fairbanks court calendar carries one case under a weekend and holiday judge. Neither the Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch nor the Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin had posted anything for Oct. 19 when they were read shortly before four in the morning, and none of the three preceding days behind either feed had changed. The Alaska Court System's weekly criminal filings report, covering Oct. 12 to Oct. 18, lists 47 cases at Fairbanks, three at Delta Junction and no section for Nenana or Healy; those counts are the report's own, and the report has been short of its own final filing day before. Nothing has been filed at Fairbanks since case 4FA-26-02117CR on Sunday. Nineteen case numbers the court prints or has printed in its own weekly report cannot be found in the public case database, and are listed with no explanation offered. Three records could not be read in full: the United States Attorney's press index refused a direct request and was read indirectly, which confirms only which releases are listed; the Daily News-Miner public safety column for Oct. 18 is behind a subscription wall; and the Fairbanks Police Department's Facebook page is behind a login wall. The open cases listing below carries 184 files, 51 of them with full charge, judge and docket detail and 133 with the summary fields the court's own records provide. A count of zero on any police feed means only that nothing had been posted at the time of reading.

entries.title: Court offices closed for the Alaska Day observance; one case on the Fairbanks calendar
body: Alaska Day falls on Oct. 18. Because that date fell on a Sunday this year, the holiday is observed on Monday, Oct. 19, and court offices across the state are closed. The Alaska Court System sets out that rule on its published holiday schedule.

The Fairbanks daily court calendar for Monday carries one case, listed under a weekend and holiday judge. It is a juvenile detention matter from Bethel rather than a Fourth Judicial District criminal case.
No new criminal case has been filed at the Fairbanks court since Sunday afternoon, and the next run of the court's weekly criminal filings report is due on Monday night.

entries.agency: Alaska State Troopers; Fairbanks Police Department
entries.title: Neither daily police feed has posted anything for Monday
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch page for Oct. 19 had published nothing when it was read at 3:52 a.m.: the page carries no date header and serves no detachment sections.
The Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin returned no entries for Oct. 19 when it was read at 3:48 a.m., and also returned no entries for Sunday, Oct. 18.

The three preceding days behind each feed were re-read and none had changed. On the trooper dispatch, D Detachment holds five items for Oct. 18, four for Oct. 17 and three for Oct. 16. On the police bulletin, Oct. 18 holds none, Oct. 17 five and Oct. 16 three.
Both feeds add entries to days already published, sometimes several days later, so a count of zero means only that nothing had been posted at the time of reading.

entries.title: Weekly criminal filings report: 47 cases at Fairbanks, three at Delta Junction, none at Nenana or Healy
body: The Alaska Court System's weekly report of criminal charges filed, covering Oct. 12 to Oct. 18 and run at 9:01 p.m. on Oct. 18, lists 47 cases filed at the Fairbanks court, three at Delta Junction and no section at all for Nenana or Healy.

The Fairbanks cases run in an unbroken series from 4FA-26-02071CR to 4FA-26-02117CR. By filing day: six on Monday, five on Tuesday, eight on Wednesday, three on Thursday, twelve on Friday, four on Saturday and nine on Sunday.

Nenana's nil return is because the report's seven-day window has rolled past the days its most recent cases were filed on, not because nothing has been filed there. The word Healy does not appear anywhere in the 62-page document, for the twenty-third week running.
The counts above are the report's own. The report has been short of its own final filing day at least once, so they are a minimum for the last day of any window.

entries.title: Nine Fairbanks cases filed on Sunday now appear in the court's weekly report
body: All nine criminal cases filed at the Fairbanks court on Sunday, Oct. 18 are printed in the weekly report run that night. Charge classes below are those recorded on the court file. Everyone named is charged, not convicted.

4FA-26-02109CR, Roderick Antoino Hill: two Class C felony counts, felony driving under the influence with two or more prior convictions and felony refusal of a chemical test with two or more prior convictions, both offence-dated Oct. 17 at Fairbanks.

4FA-26-02110CR and 4FA-26-02111CR, Timothy Leland Phillippe: one Class C felony count of theft in the second degree, value $750 to $24,999, and one Class C felony count of burglary in the second degree, both offence-dated Sept. 1 at Fairbanks.
4FA-26-02112CR, Helena J Cole: one count recorded as a charging document pending or not filed, with no degree of offence stated and an offence location of North Pole.

4FA-26-02113CR, Moses Alejandro Luke Gutierrez: two Class A misdemeanour counts, assault in the fourth degree recorded as domestic violence related, and driving under the influence, both offence-dated Oct. 18 at Fairbanks. The report records a blood alcohol content of .067.

4FA-26-02114CR, Nolan Iver Peterson: two Class C felony counts of theft in the second degree involving an access device or identification document and one Class A misdemeanour count of theft in the third degree of mail, all offence-dated Oct. 17 at Fairbanks.

4FA-26-02115CR, Christine Marie Guzman: one Class A misdemeanour count of criminal trespass in the first degree and one Class B misdemeanour count of criminal mischief in the fifth degree, both recorded as domestic violence related and offence-dated Oct. 17 at Fairbanks.

4FA-26-02116CR, Derek Storm Kelly: five counts, all offence-dated Oct. 17 at North Pole - one Class B misdemeanour of criminal trespass in the second degree, three Class A misdemeanour counts of assault in the fourth degree and one Class B misdemeanour of violating conditions of release.

4FA-26-02117CR, Julia Ann Pitka: six counts offence-dated Oct. 17 at Fairbanks, including one Class B felony of misconduct involving a controlled substance in the third degree, two Class C felony counts of theft in the second degree involving an access device or identification document, a Class A misdemeanour count of theft of mail, a Class A misdemeanour drug possession count and a Class A misdemeanour count of violating a condition of release for a felony.

entries.title: Court record now gives North Pole as the offence location in a case with no charge filed
body: The weekly criminal filings report records an offence location of North Pole against case 4FA-26-02112CR, Helena J Cole, which was filed on Oct. 18.

The single count on that file is still recorded as a charging document pending or not filed, with no statute and no degree of offence, so no charge class is stated here. The case is listed as open before judge Seekins with an arraignment set for Oct. 23.
The trooper dispatch entry behind the arrest records the incident location as Fairbanks. The two records disagree about the place and both are reported here.

entries.title: A trial week set for Monday was reset, and hearing dates in a tampering case have changed again
body: Case 4FA-26-01818CR, William Bruce Ostlund, carried a scheduled trial week for Oct. 19 in Courtroom 403. That setting is recorded as reset. A bail hearing stands for Oct. 20, a calendar call for Nov. 17 and a trial week for Nov. 30.

Case 4FA-26-01896CR, Amanda Elizabeth Moff, charged with one Class C felony count of tampering with physical evidence, now records the omnibus hearing of Dec. 1 and the trial week of Dec. 14 as reset, with an omnibus hearing on Nov. 5 and a trial week of Nov. 23 standing in their place. The case judge field reads not assigned. Nothing has been added to the docket on that file since Oct. 7.
No case on the open list carries a docket entry dated Oct. 19.

entries.title: Delta Junction teenager reported missing on Oct. 16 has been found
body: The Alaska State Troopers reported a 14-year-old Delta Junction resident missing on Oct. 16, after she was discovered missing from her home that morning. Troopers recorded that she appeared to have left intentionally and might be in Fairbanks.
The dispatch entry has since been updated to record that she has been found. She is a juvenile and is not named here.

entries.title: Two traffic collisions drew fire and medical crews on Sunday, one for more than three hours
body: The Fairbanks Emergency Communications Center dispatch log records a traffic collision at 1012 Gold Mine Trail at 6:49 p.m. on Oct. 18, closed after three hours and twenty-six minutes, with a battalion chief, an engine, a medic unit, a rescue unit and two squads assigned.
A second traffic collision at Spring Glade Road and Wideview Road at 7:59 a.m. the same day was closed after an hour and twelve minutes, with the same complement of units.

Neither collision appears in the trooper dispatch, the police bulletin or any court filing read on Oct. 19. This log records fire and medical responses only and carries no police or crime incident type.
